headline: Single-cell multiomics links 3D genome and isoform structure to cell-type regulation
label: Single Cell Multiomics Methods
summary: Joint profiling of 3D chromatin, isoforms, haplotype copy number and spatial gradients now resolves regulatory and structural features within cell types.
synthesis: The dominant thread is cell-type resolution of regulatory and structural features from single-cell or deconvolved profiles. Several items extend this to new layers: CNVeil infers haplotype-specific copy number from scDNA-seq and reveals subclonal structure hidden in total copy number profiles; Fullscope-seq maps isoform usage by cell type and layer in primate brain; GAGE-seq jointly captures 3D chromatin and expression in Alzheimer's postmortem brain, with Hicformer linking 3D genome features to expression. A multi-omic atlas of human RPE and choroid (102 donors) links AMD GWAS variants to LIPG and COL4A3, and a retina atlas spans 23 cell types across chromatin accessibility, methylation and 3D architecture. Computational advances include HiC2Self denoising of single-cell Hi-C, cellGeometry deconvolution of bulk RNA-seq, and BayesPrism-derived cell-type expression targets for sequence-to-expression models. What is new is the joint measurement of genome structure, isoform and haplotype state within defined cell types rather than bulk averages.
